data.text: All the pieces are in place. The evidence chain is complete:

data.error: category must be one of: dhcp, dns, hardware, monitoring, routing, service, wan

data.cause: dns1.lan's resolver rate-limits the whole LAN as a single /24 bucket at only 20 q/s (ratelimit_subnet_len_ipv4: 24), so ordinary bursts a few times a day cause it to drop queries; clients then fall back to their second server gw.lan, whose unbound private-address filtering strips the forwarded .lan answers and returns an empty NOERROR, which the monitor reports as getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND until the burst passes.
evidence: dig @10.20.0.3 nas.lan on mon.lan: NOERROR with answer A 10.20.0.50 but TTL of only 10 seconds — every client re-queries dns1 constantly.
dig @10.20.0.1 nas.lan on mon.lan: NOERROR with ANSWER: 0 — the fallback server returns an empty answer, indistinguishable from NXDOMAIN to getaddrinfo (ENOTFOUND).
drill nas.lan @127.0.0.1 on gw.lan: same empty NOERROR, confirming gw's own resolver is the source, not a forwarding failure.
/opt/primary-dns/config.yaml on dns1.lan: ratelimit: 20 with ratelimit_subnet_len_ipv4: 24 — one shared bucket for all clients in 10.20.0.0/24.

journalctl -u primary-dns on dns1.lan: three separate 'ratelimit: 10.20.0.0/24 exceeded 20 q/s, dropping N queries' events today (02:14, 09:41, 13:02), each back under limit within ~30 seconds — matching 'a few times a day, self-clearing'.
/var/unbound/unbound.conf on gw.lan: forwards name lan. to 10.20.0.3 but also sets private-address: 10.0.0.0/8, so forwarded .lan answers (10.20.0.50) are filtered out before being served.
/etc/resolv.conf on mon.lan: nameserver order 10.20.0.3 then 10.20.0.1 — clients fall back to gw.lan exactly when dns1 drops their query.
Internet names unaffected because public-name answers from the DoH upstream carry no private addresses and pass gw's filtering.
data.recommendation: On dns1.lan, stop rate-limiting local .lan lookups as one /24 bucket: set ratelimit_subnet_len_ipv4 to 32 (per-client buckets) or raise ratelimit well above normal burst levels. Additionally, fix gw.lan's unbound so its private-address filtering doesn't strip the forwarded .lan zone (serve .lan via local-zone/local-data instead), so the fallback server returns real answers rather than empty NOERRORs.
data.detail: primary-dns per-subnet rate limiter drops burst queries for .lan names
